rows.title: Job scanner counts a tech phrase and each of its words as separate keywords (CI/CD also as CI and CD)
rows.summary: Now: when a job posting contains one of the listed tech phrases ('CI/CD', 'machine learning'), the phrase counts as one keyword. Its words ('CI', 'CD', 'machine', 'learning') are no longer counted a second time in the match percentage, and '+' no longer offers them for Skills. A word the posting also uses on its own (for example 'learning' elsewhere in the text) is still a keyword. One-word phrases ('frontend') are unaffected. The review changed how the words are removed: a word loses a count only where it was read as a separate word inside that phrase. Before, 'machine learning-based ranking with a continuous learning culture' also dropped the separate word 'learning'. The token rule now lives in one helper, jobKeywordOf, which extractJobKeywords uses both for counting and for reading the words inside a phrase.
rows.failfirst_run: 36534214985 (2663b23: 3 fail without the fix, pass with it); review 36536345765 (77eae5b: 2 fail without, pass with)

rows.title: Job scanner reads pay figures ('$150K–$180K') as missing keywords that '+' writes into Skills
rows.summary: Now: a figure is no job keyword. That covers plain numbers, '5+', numbers with a K/M/B suffix ('150K', '1.5M', '2B+') and ranges joined by a hyphen, with or without a suffix ('120k-140k', '150-180K', '120000-150000', '3-5' years, '12-15'). A pay range such as '$150K–$180K' or '120,000-150,000' is never listed under Missing Keywords, never lowers the match, and '+' never writes it into Skills. Tech names with digits ('S3', 'EC2', '5G', 'Web3') are still keywords, and a guard test pins that. The review extended af627d3, which caught only figures with a K/M/B suffix: plain ranges such as '$120000-150000', '120,000-150,000' (read as '000-150') and '3-5 years' were still keywords.
rows.failfirst_run: 36534214985 (af627d3: 2 fail without the fix, pass with it); review 36536345765 (77eae5b: 2 fail without, pass with)

issues.issue: The new regex skipped a figure only when it had a K/M/B suffix. '$120000-150000' stayed the keyword '120000-150000', '120,000-150,000' stayed '000-150', '3-5 years' stayed '3-5' and '12-15 LPA' stayed '12-15'. All of these were always missing from the résumé and '+' wrote them into Skills.
issues.resolution: fixed in 77eae5b: one figure rule (digits, optional decimals, optional K/M/B, ranges joined by a hyphen, optional '+'); fail-first run 36536345765

issues.issue: Each word lost one count for every regex match of the phrase, even where the tokenizer had not read that word as a separate token. In 'machine learning-based … continuous learning' the token was 'learning-based', so the separate 'learning' was deleted. The same happened with '#machine learning … machine vision' and 'machine'. This broke the fix's own rule that a word the posting also uses on its own stays a keyword.
issues.resolution: fixed in 77eae5b: the tokens around each match are read with the same rule (jobKeywordOf), and a word loses a count only when it is one of them; fail-first run 36536345765

issues.issue: Figure rule missed ranges without a K/M/B suffix
Phrase subtraction removed a word's standalone use when the phrase ran into a hyphenated or '#'-prefixed token

Pay vocabulary around a figure ('USD', 'hr', 'yr', 'LPA', 'Salary', 'Pay') is still read as keywords. This is not the figure bug: those words are missing from the stop list. Adding them risks dropping real keywords (for example 'Payroll', 'Pay' for a payments role).
issues.resolution: not fixed; noted for a later hunt as a stop-list product call

notes: Both fixer commits change only extractJobKeywords in src/utils/atsChecker.js. Its only caller is matchResumeWithJob, used by the ATS panel's job match. Nothing is stored, so there is no old-data or exporter impact. I read the fail-first logs of run 36534214985: 2663b23 had '# fail 3' and af627d3 had '# fail 2' with the diff reversed, and both passed with the fix restored. Review fix 77eae5b: fail-first '# fail 2' and named-tests run 36536345765 green (lint and 14 ATS/knowledge test files). Playwright, Cypress, build and the full suite were not run, so the batch gate still has to run them. No tests were run locally; extractJobKeywords was only called directly with node on sample postings.
